theorems.name: Parallel trends identifies the ATT (difference-in-differences)
theorems.description: Two-period, two-group difference-in-differences with a binary treatment and no covariates: if the two groups' untreated potential outcome has the same mean change over time (parallel trends, stated as an equality of conditional means on Y(0)), then the ATT equals the difference-in-differences contrast of four conditional means of the OBSERVED outcome (Econometrics.Model.att_eq_didContrast). The observability discipline is carried by the types rather than by a comment: `att` takes a `Model` (potential outcomes) and reads the counterfactual Y(0) on treated units, while `didContrast` takes an `Observed` (treatment group + realized outcomes, counterfactuals absent from the structure), so the theorem is literally the statement that a counterfactual functional equals one that reads no counterfactual. Both sides still take the population measure as an argument, so this is the 'reads no counterfactual' half of identification and NOT the stronger 'depends only on the law of the observables', which needs the pushforward as carrier. Also NOT proved: conditional parallel trends, covariate adjustment, staggered adoption, repeated cross sections, or anything about two-way fixed-effects estimators under heterogeneous timing.

code.lean:
import Econometrics.Identification.DiD

open MeasureTheory Econometrics

/-- Parallel trends identifies the ATT: the average treatment effect on the treated,
a functional of unobservable potential outcomes, equals the difference-in-differences
contrast, a functional of the observed data alone. -/
theorem did_parallel_trends_identifies_att
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (m : Econometrics.Model Ω)
    (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
    (hT : MeasurableSet m.treated)
    (h₁ : MeasureTheory.Integrable (m.Y true Econometrics.Period.post) μ)
    (h₀ : MeasureTheory.Integrable (m.Y false Econometrics.Period.post) μ)
    (hpre : MeasureTheory.Integrable (m.Y false Econometrics.Period.pre) μ)
    (hPT : m.ParallelTrends μ) :
    m.att μ = m.observed.didContrast μ :=
  Econometrics.Model.att_eq_didContrast m μ hT h₁ h₀ hpre hPT

metadata.formalization_scope: Full derivation, phase 0 (2026-08-10). The formal statement is the canonical two-period/two-group DiD identification result and nothing wider. Encoding: conditioning is ProbabilityTheory.cond (the conditional MEASURE given an event), so a conditional mean is the integral against mu[|s]; this is what the informal theorem says and it keeps the four observable means literally four integrals. The sigma-algebra encoding via MeasureTheory.condExp is what covariate conditioning (RDD, IV) will need, and the bridge between the two is deferred to phase 1 — see docs/phase0-verdict.md. DISCLOSURE, the one place the formal statement is weaker than the phrase 'identified': Observed omits the potential outcomes, so didContrast provably reads no counterfactual, but both sides take the population measure mu on the same Omega, so the statement does not yet say the estimand depends only on the observable LAW. Restating it over the pushforward of (outcome, treated) is a declared phase-1 upgrade, tracked in docs/phase0-verdict.md. The realization rule (nobody treated pre-period; each unit realizes its assigned arm post-period) is a DEFINITION, Model.observed, written with Set.indicator so no decidability instance is needed; the two bridge lemmas DERIVE the observed-equals-potential identities almost-everywhere from ProbabilityTheory.ae_cond_mem rather than assuming them. One adapter lemma was needed and is absent from Mathlib at the pin: MeasureTheory.Integrable.cond (integrability survives conditioning), three lines, field-neutral, staged as a ForMathlib candidate. Hypotheses are the minimal set the proof consumes: measurability of the treated set, integrability of the three potential outcomes that appear, and parallel trends — no finiteness or probability-measure assumption on mu was required. Axioms-clean.
